question.text: A famous part of the army of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth were the Winged Hussars, an elite cavalry unit that lifted the Ottoman siege of this present-day European country's capital city of Vienna.

swap.leadin: This dynasty converted the Schonbrunn (shurn-brun) Palace from a hunting lodge to the permanent imperial summer residence where Franz Joseph died.

question.text: A Congress in this Austrian city attempted to create a "balance of power" in Europe after Napoleon's defeat.
question.clue: Many of this city's parks were built under its mayor Karl Lueger, whose anti-Semitic rhetoric likely inspired one-time resident Adolf Hitler.

swap.leadin: His death and that of his wife Sophie prompted the July Crisis.

question.text: The ascension of this only female ruler of the Holy Roman Empire to the throne would have violated Salic Law, so her father negotiated the Pragmatic Succession to legitimize it.
question.clue: This leader lost control of Silesia when the Pragmatic Sanction, set up by her father, Charles VI, was violated by Prussia.

question.leadin: This empire used "K.U.K." as its official abbreviation on ships and various articles of state in order to reflect political realities of split power.
question.text: Name this European empire that was formed by a namesake 1867 compromise. It was one of the members of the pre-World War I Triple Alliance along with Italy and the German Empire.
question.clue: The phrase "k.u.k" was used as a term for this country's system of government after the Ausgleich.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Kingdom of Italy.
swap.text: The Kingdom of Italy fought against this nation and its ally Germany at the Battle of Caporetto which was a decisive victory for this nation. This nation used the acronym k.u.k to represent its dual monarchy.
swap.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or The Kingdoms and Lands Represented in the Imperial Council and the Lands of the Holy Hungarian Crown of St. Stephen; do not accept or prompt on “Austria” or “Hungary” or “Austrian Empire”]
swap.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about self-identified enlightened despots.
question.text: When asked his thoughts on the American Revolution, this Austrian ruler and enlightened despot replied, "Madam, it is my trade to be a King". This son of Maria Theresa liberalized the curriculum of the University of Vienna and abolished the Robot Patent.
question.clue: His first wife Isabella of Parma died of smallpox long before that blunder in the Battle of Karansebes.

swap.text: This 1711 declaration said that the daughters of Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI had precedence in succession over the heirs of former emperors Leopold I and Joseph I.

swap.leadin: A rigged referendum used to bring about this event featured a ballot with a large, centered "yes" circle and a smaller "no" circle to the right.
swap.text: Name this 1938 event in which Nazi Germany annexed its southern neighbor. Kurt Schuschnigg ("SHOOSH-nig") was forced to resign for opposing this event.

question.text: A more famous royal figure assassinated by Serbian nationalists was this Archduke, the heir to the Austrian throne, who was assassinated in Sarajevo.

question.answerHtml: Franz Conrad von Hoetzendorf [or Franz Xaver Josef Conrad von Hoetzendorf; accept von Hoetzendorf]
